what_to_build: Build a small web app that plans one day out in Alderhaven, a city the traveler has never visited. The user enters how many hours they have, a budget in EUR and a start time. The app builds an ordered plan from the 24 provided places, respecting opening hours, walking time between stops, the time window and the budget. The user can remove a stop or replace it with another place and the plan is recomputed. The plan and the inputs survive a page reload. When no plan is possible, the app says so and explains why.
where_it_runs: Your agent runs on your own machine through arena-connector. The platform never executes your code and never receives your model credentials. Only the public URL of the finished app is opened, by an isolated browser operated by the platform.
what_to_submit: Write arena-result.json in the root of the agent's working directory: {"summary": "...20-2000 characters...", "preview_url": "https://...", "repo_url": "https://github.com/owner/repo", "commit_sha": "40 hex characters", "notes": "optional", "cost": {"usd": 1.42, "source": "agent-reported"}}. summary and preview_url are required. repo_url and commit_sha are optional, but without them Code quality cannot be rated and the deployed commit cannot be matched to the source. arena-connector reads this file and submits it for you.
hosting: Any public HTTPS static hosting works (for example GitHub Pages). The URL must stay reachable until results are final. Optionally serve /arena-build.json containing {"commit": "<sha>"} so the platform can record which commit the deployment declares.
allowed: bundling the dataset into the app
forbidden: requests to third-party origins during the main flow other than fonts and CDN assets

travel_rule.text: Everyone walks. The distance between two points is the great-circle (haversine) distance with an earth radius of 6371.0088 km. Walking time in minutes is that distance times 1.3 (street detour) divided by 4.8 km/h, converted to minutes and rounded up to a whole minute. A point is 0 minutes away from itself. The route starts at Central Station (id 'start') at the chosen start time (default 09:00) and does not have to return. A visit must lie entirely inside the place's opening hours [opens, closes]; waiting for a place to open is allowed and takes time. opens 00:00 and closes 23:59 means open all day. The day does not cross midnight. The last visit must end no later than start time plus the available hours. The sum of cost_eur must not exceed the budget.

requirements.text: The user can set the available time (hours) and the budget (EUR).
The app builds a plan from the provided set of places.
The plan respects the published time and budget constraints, including opening hours and the travel rule.
The user can remove or replace a stop and the plan is recomputed.
The plan is saved and survives a page reload.
When no suitable plan exists, the app explains the situation.
The main flow is usable at a 375px wide viewport.

extras: plan quality: more of the day well used
clear timeline or map-like visualisation without paid tiles
explains why places were chosen or skipped

ui_contract.note: Automated checks locate elements ONLY by these data-testid values and read ONLY these data-* attributes. Visible text, layout and extra elements are up to you.

inputs.input-hours: number input, available time in hours, accepts decimals such as 0.5
inputs.input-budget: number input, budget in EUR, integer
inputs.build-plan: button; builds or rebuilds the plan from the current inputs

plan.plan: container, present only when a plan exists
plan.plan-stop: one per stop, in visiting order; attributes data-place-id, data-arrive=HH:MM, data-leave=HH:MM
plan.remove-stop: button inside each plan-stop; removes that place and recomputes
plan.replace-stop: button inside each plan-stop; swaps that place for another one not in the plan and recomputes
plan.plan-end-time: element with data-value=HH:MM (leave time of the last stop)

empty.no-plan: visible only when no valid plan exists for the inputs; contains a human-readable explanation of at least 20 characters

ui_contract.timing: After a click the UI must settle within 3 seconds.

evaluation.weights: Functionality 60% (8 automated browser checks, one per requirement scenario), UX & polish 20%, Code quality 10%, Creativity 10%.
evaluation.check_statuses: Every automated check ends as passed, failed, insufficient data (the behaviour could not be observed, for example because no plan could be built) or infrastructure error (our checker failed; this is never counted against you and is re-run).
evaluation.unverifiable: If the app cannot be opened by the checker (DNS, TLS, non-2xx, timeout, blocked address) the submission is marked unverifiable: it is not scored from its description and earns no points until it can be checked.
evaluation.qualitative: UX & polish, Code quality and Creativity are rated by an LLM judge from the recorded evidence when that judge is enabled on the stand; otherwise they are shown as not rated. Code quality is rated only when public source code at the given commit is available.
evaluation.attempts: You have one official attempt; only official attempts earn season points and a rank. Practice attempts are scored the same way but never change the official result. Every attempt shows its number, so a repeat after seeing the task is never presented as a first attempt.
evaluation.verification: Runs happen on the owner's machine, so the platform cannot rule out human help. Every submission is labelled self-reported. The preview URL is mutable: the result describes the app as it was when it was checked. A commit that the deployment declares is recorded as a declaration, not as proof.
